title: Yat Ga Mein with Meat, Fish, or Poultry

content.title: About
content.content: Yat Ga Mein is a classic Chinese stir‑fried noodle dish made with soy‑based sauce, vegetables and a choice of protein – beef, pork, chicken, duck or fish. It features a savory‑sweet sauce, tender noodles and crisp vegetables.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Yat Ga Mein is a popular street‑food item across China and Southeast Asia.
The name comes from Cantonese “Yat Ga” (一加) meaning “one plus”, referring to the optional addition of any meat.
Traditional recipes use egg noodles, though rice or wheat noodles are sometimes substituted.
A fried egg is often placed on top for extra richness.
The sauce is typically made from soy sauce, oyster sauce, a touch of sugar and sesame oil.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Choosing meat, fish or poultry provides complete protein essential for muscle repair and growth.

items.title: Iron source
items.content: Red meats and organ meats commonly used in the dish are good sources of iron, supporting healthy blood.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The dish supplies B1, B2, B6 and B12 vitamins that aid energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Fiber from vegetables
items.content: Added vegetables such as onions, carrots and peppers increase dietary fiber, promoting digestion.

items.title: Low added sugar
items.content: Despite a mildly sweet sauce, the overall sugar content remains modest.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Soy and oyster sauces are salty; people with hypertension should watch portion size.

items.title: Soy allergy
items.content: Soy sauce can trigger allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Fatty meat cuts
items.content: Using fattier cuts of pork or beef raises calories and saturated fat levels.

items.title: Potential fish toxins
items.content: When fish is used, ensure it is fresh to avoid food‑borne illness.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the dish hot, straight from the wok. Garnish with fresh cilantro, lime wedges, or sliced chili for extra flavor. Optional toppings include a fried egg, toasted sesame seeds or cucumber ribbons.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Best enjoyed within 2–3 hours of cooking. Leftovers should be stored in an airtight container in the refrigerator and consumed within 24 hours, reheating quickly in a pan or microwave.
